core_obligations: Record the three inputs: the description of the reduction of a formal algebraic space, the construction of the reduced induced closed subspace, and the definition of the completion (proof lines 3263-3269).

Observe that both sides are reduced algebraic spaces satisfying the same mapping property: a morphism from a reduced algebraic space factors through them if and only if its image lies in the closed subset (proof lines 3269-3273).
Conclude that the two agree (proof lines 3273).
proof_roadmap: Comparison of mapping properties and conclusion (proof lines 3269-3273).
difficulty_reason: For an algebraic space X and a closed subset T, the lemma asserts that the reduction of the completion of X along T is the reduced induced closed subspace corresponding to T (statement lines 3254-3261). The proof does not compute with the construction of the completion but compares universal properties: it cites the description of the reduction of a formal algebraic space, the definition of the reduced induced closed subspace and the definition of the completion, and observes that both sides are reduced algebraic spaces characterised by the same mapping property, namely that a morphism from a reduced algebraic space factors through them exactly when its image lies in T (proof lines 3263-3273). The claim is H2: the argument is short but it is a complete identification of two objects by their universal properties, and each of the three inputs is named.
